title: Jake Ferguson was listed as a “DNP” on the estimated practice report Monday.
text: Even though the team held a walkthrough ahead of their Thanksgiving matchup against the Eagles, the fact that Ferguson has yet to practice after injuring his ankle two weeks ago spells trouble for his potential availability in Week 12. Brevyn Spann-Ford and Luke Schoonmaker appear to be looking at another game atop the depth chart, with volume through the air most likely to concentrate further on CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. - Mark Garcia

title: Seahawks placed RB George Holani (knee) on injured reserve.
text: The move hurts far less than it would have earlier in the season when both Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price were unavailable. The change of pace option and special teams ace will now miss the next four games, at minimum, placing him in line to potentially return for Week 16 as the Seahawks make their final push toward the postseason. - Mark Garcia

title: Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle) was listed as limited on Monday’s estimated injury report.
text: Kincaid missed Week 11’s game against the Dolphins with the same set of injuries despite being questionable entering the weekend. It’s quite possible the decision to sit him against the one-win Dolphins was more of a precautionary one ahead of the Bills’ Week 12 matchup against the Chiefs. We’ll see how the rest of his week unfolds, but Kincaid practicing in any capacity this week should be viewed as a good sign for his availability. - Zachary Krueger

title: Micah Parson has been cleared to return for the Packers’ Week 12 game against the Rams.
text: This one game a bit earlier than expected. While the hope was Parsons would return on Wednesday, the star pass rusher was listed as a limited participant in Monday’s practice, leaving some doubt as to whether or not he would be cleared for a return. Now, the Packers get back their 2025 sack leader who last played in Week 15 of last season, when he suffered a torn ACL on the road against the Broncos. Parsons will provide an immediate boost to a defense that currently ranks 16th in points allowed but eighth in passing yards allowed per game. They are also tied for the seventh-most team sacks in

title: Kenneth Walker (groin) was listed as DNP on Monday’s estimated injury report.
text: This wasn’t the news fantasy managers were looking for after going without Walker for each of the last two weeks. The Chiefs’ RB1 has been sidelined with a groin injury he suffered ahead of Week 10’s game against the Falcons, but there was early hope it would be a one-game absence. It was widely believed the decision to sit him against the woeful Cardinals was made to give him additional time to heal up before Week 12’s game against the Bills, but Monday’s DNP now draws his availability against Buffalo into question. The Chiefs didn’t officially practice today, but Walker would not have been p

title: Daniel Jones has cleared waivers and is now free to sign with any team.
text: Now that he has passed through waivers, Jones is officially a free agent and is free to sign with any team. While plenty of QB-needy teams could reach out for his services, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported early Monday that Jones will likely wait to sign with a new team and may leave the door open to signing with a contender later in the season that suddenly finds itself in need of a starting QB. - Zachary Krueger

title: Quinyon Mitchell (hamstring) did not practice on Monday.
text: It was an estimated session. Mitchell talked with reporters after leaving Sunday’s game with the hamstring ailment, implying it wasn’t a super serious injury. Still, on a short week, his status is up in the air. If he were ruled out, it would only help CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens on Thanksgiving. - Rivers McCown

title: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) is practicing in full ahead of Philadelphia’s Thursday game against the Cowboys.
text: We’re expecting the Eagles to force-feed Smith once more after his 57 percent target share on Sunday, leaving him as a plausible WR2 in an elevated matchup against the Cowboys defense. - Rivers McCown

title: Will Shipley (foot/illness) was limited in Monday’s practice.
text: It was an estimated session and exactly the same listing he had on Friday. As he was practicing on a limited basis before the illness (and before being activated off injured reserve last Saturday), we’ll assume he has a fairly good chance to suit up on Thursday. - Rivers McCown

title: Dallas Goedert (shin) was limited in Monday’s practice.
text: It’s a new (estimated) listing after his one-catch outing against the Steelers. Goedert was at least set up with a Joe Milton #RevengeGame script against a weak Cowboys defense this week to try to rebound, but it will be hard to rely on him as a streamer TE1 if healthy. We’ll see if he can get to the second part of that statement tomorrow. - Rivers McCown

title: Dallas Goedert (shin) was listed as a limited participant on Monday’s estimated practice report.
text: Likely nothing to see here as the veteran tight end prepares for a divisional matchup against the Cowboys on Thanksgiving. Goedert’s 38-yard reception last week against the Steelers was his longer catch since Week 1, although the fact it was his only grab is troubling considering it was the first game with a healthy DeVonta Smith in a month. Goedert has been relegated to a top end TE2 against the Cowboys. - Mark Garcia

title: Saquon Barkley (neck/illness) was listed as a limited participant on Monday’s estimated practice report.
text: Barkley should be good to go for the team’s Thanksgiving showdown against the Cowboys Thursday despite the dual-tag designation. The veteran workhorse is coming off one of his best performances of the season against the Steelers, leading the team to their first win in two calendar months. - Mark Garcia

title: Commanders declared CB Amik Robertson, QB Athan Kaliakmanis, RB Robert Henry Jr., Ricky Barber, and G Tanoa Togiai inactive for Week 11 against the Bengals.
text: - Mark Garcia

title: Bengals declared S Kyle Dugger, OL Myles Hinton, DL Landon Robinson, OL Dalton Risner, and TE Cam Grandy inactive for Week 11 against the Commanders.
text: - Mark Garcia

title: Jayden Daniels (left elbow/left hand) is practicing in full for Week 12 against the Cardinals.
text: Daniels’ left elbow issue is obviously not new, but the left hand injury is. That said, he is practicing in full and gets an exceptionally soft matchup against the Cardinals’ defense this week. Daniels is a high-end QB1, as usual. - Nic Bodiford

title: Denzel Boston (quad) did not practice on Wednesday.
text: Boston continues to rack up lower-body injuries, though he tends to play through them. He dealt with a toe injury last week, catching just one pass for 16 yards. His practice participation is worth tracking closely this week. - Nic Bodiford

title: Harold Fannin (groin) was limited on Wednesday.
text: Fannin has been dealing with this groin injury since Week 9, but it has not impacted his productivity. Fannin is a locked-in TE1 against the Raiders in Week 12. Ideally, he will upgrade to full participation by the end of the week. - Nic Bodiford

title: Michael Mayer (back) is practicing in full for Week 12 against the Browns.
text: Mayer injured his back in the Raiders’ Week 11 loss to the Broncos, but he is evidently good to go this week. Brock Bowers (ankle) was limited today, tentatively putting him on track to face the Browns this weekend. - Nic Bodiford

title: Brock Bowers (ankle) was limited on Wednesday.
text: Bowers closed last week with two limited sessions, listed with ankle and quad injuries. Fortunately, the quad injury is no longer an issue. He is tentatively on track to play in Week 12 against the Browns. Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said he is optimistic that Bowers will play this weekend, adding that having a bye in Week 13 will not factor into whether Bowers suits up this week. - Nic Bodiford

title: Jahan Dotson (hamstring) did not practice on Wednesday.
text: Dotson and Zachariah Branch (hamstring) both missed Wednesday’s practice. Dotson is not relevant in 12-team leagues, and Branch has earned just 12 targets this season. Neither player is consequential. - Nic Bodiford

title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that coach Mike McCarthy “has the full support” of the Steelers’ organization and the team is “not planning to make any immediate changes.”
text: McCarthy can rest easy knowing that the organization fully backs him. Rapoport’s “immediate changes” phrasing does allow room for interpretation, though. Perhaps the team could move on in the offseason. Until then, McCarthy will roll with Mason Rudolph as his starting quarterback. They face the Broncos on Friday. - Nic Bodiford

title: Carson Beck (back) did not practice on Wednesday.
text: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said Beck has been steadily improving since back spasms hit him late in Thursday’s practice. The team is taking it one day at a time with him. The team is preparing to start Josh Johnson in Week 12 against the Commanders this week. - Nic Bodiford

title: Cardinals claimed QB Kedon Slovis off waivers.
text: The former Raven is now a Cardinal. He was notably on Arizona’s roster last summer. Slovis could end up taking live reps, pending Carson Beck’s (back) health and Josh Johnson’s performance, but he would only be a QB2/3 in that instance. - Nic Bodiford

title: Chargers claimed CB Avery Smith off waivers.
text: The Chargers traded Smith to the Seahawks earlier this year. The Seahawks waived him on Tuesday. Whether Smith plays meaningful snaps remains to be seen, but he is familiar with the system. - Nic Bodiford

title: Rachaad White (heel) is practicing in full for Week 12 against the Cardinals.
text: White dealt with this issue last week, but managed to be active on Monday night. He should be fine for backup duties in Week 1 2 against the Cardinals, though Jacory Croskey-Merritt is likely the only fantasy starter in this backfield. - Nic Bodiford

title: Treylon Burks (foot) was limited on Wednesday.
text: Burks continues to play through his foot injury, albeit mostly ineffectively. He is a boom-bust downfield wide receiver who faces a tremendously soft Cardinals pass defense this week. Burks does not need to be in 12-team lineups. - Nic Bodiford

title: Jordan Addison (thumb) did not practice Wednesday.
text: Addison has yet to practice since undergoing thumb surgery last week. Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell said Monday that the 24-year-old may not “necessarily” be back in Week 12 against the Falcons. Tai Felton will continue to get increased reps with Addison out. - Aditya Fuldeore

title: Christian Darrisaw (shoulder) did not practice Wednesday.
text: Darrisaw seemingly re-injured his shoulder in the Vikings’ Week 11 loss to the 49ers. Minnesota just held a walk-through, but the franchise left tackle starts out not practicing. He is truly questionable ahead of Week 12 against the Falcons. - Aditya Fuldeore

title: Tai Felton (hip) was limited in Wednesday’s walk-through.
text: Felton pops up on the injury report with a limited listing as he deals with a hip injury. The second-year wide receiver saw a team-high 12 targets in Week 11 against the 49ers and has seen increased opportunities with Jordan Addison still dealing with a thumb injury. Also limited was Myles Price (knee/groin). Both Price and Felton offer limited deep-league upside with Addison out. Felton is the receiver to roster, if you must. - Aditya Fuldeore

title: Kyler Murray (hamstring) was limited in Wednesday’s walk-through.
text: Murray was listed as a limited participant for the Vikings’ walk-through practice. Since going down with a hamstring injury, Murray’s starting role has been taken over by Kirk Cousins. Even if Murray is good to go for Week 12, he is likely to be in the backup role to Cousins against the Falcons. - Aditya Fuldeore

title: Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle) is questionable for Week 12 against the Chiefs.
text: Kincaid was limited in practice all week but said he would most likely play. The Bills also listed Christian Benford (groin), T.J. Sanders (shoulder), O’Cyrus Torrence (ankle), and Dorian Williams (calf) as limited for Thursday night after a week of limited practices for each player. - Aditya Fuldeore

title: Josh Jacobs (thumb) is inactive for Week 12 against the Rams.
text: Jacobs was limited in the Packers’ practices this week, but is not ready to return to play just yet. Kaleb Johnson and MarShawn Lloyd will split the backfield opportunities in his absence. The Packers also declared LB Zaire Franklin, OL Jager Burton, OL Donovan Jennings, and OL Mekhi Becton inactive for Week 12 against the Rams. - Aditya Fuldeore

title: NFL Insider Tom Pelissero reports Kyren Williams “has been battling turf toe for the past month.”
text: Williams was on the Rams’ injury report this week with a toe injury before getting cleared off the report before Wednesday. Pelissero reveals that Williams told him he has been battling turf toe for the past month. This stretch coincides with Blake Corum’s increased opportunities while Williams has seen his role reduced to more of a backfield split. Williams will continue to play through the injury, but expect Corum to still be heavily involved as a result. - Aditya Fuldeore

title: Micah Parsons (knee) is active for Week 12 against the Rams.
text: Parsons is officially back after the Packers activated him off the PUP list this week. He is back nearly a year after suffering a torn ACL last season, making his debut on Thanksgiving eve against the Rams. The Packers pass rush gets a boost with the return of the five-time Pro Bowler this week. - Aditya Fuldeore

title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Christian Watson has entered the league’s concussion protocol.
text: Watson exited in the second quarter of Wednesday’s game against the Rams after taking a helmet-to-helmet hit from Rams safety Kamren Kinchens. The hard hit left Watson on the ground for an extended period before he eventually got up on his own and went to the locker room. Watson was ruled out after halftime and now has to clear concussion protocol to play in Week 13’s game against the Saints. With extended time to clear protocol, Watson should have a decent chance of clearing protocol. We will be tracking his practice status throughout next week. - Zachary Krueger

title: Colby Parkinson caught both targets for minus one yard in the Rams’ Week 12 win over the Packers.
text: Parkinson somehow lost a yard on two reception despite the team losing both Tyler Higbee and Davis Allen to injury, the latter of whom departed in the first half and the former of whom left at the beginning of the fourth quarter. The Rams completely controlled the flow of the game after Packers receiver Christian Watson departed with a concussion following a vicious targeting hit down the sideline just before the half, eventually leading to 47 total team carries to just 23 Matthew Stafford pass attempts. The Rams have some things to figure out given the sheer number of bodies missing after als

title: Konata Mumpfield caught 4-of-5 targets for 69 yards in the Rams’ Week 12 win over the Packers.
text: Mumpfield saw a team-high five targets and turned them into a team-leading 69 yards in one of the more dominant performances of the season. Despite the seemingly close score, the Rams jumped out to an early 13-3 lead while holding the Packers to only 44 total offensive plays run from scrimmage. The inability of the Packers to move the football resulted in additional time of possession for the Rams, which they used to notch 47 rush attempts to just 23 Matthew Stafford pass attempts, eight of which were directed at the backfield duo of Blake Corum and Kyren Williams. Mumpfield remains the player

title: Kyren Williams rushed 12 times for 46 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 12 win over the Packers, adding 19 yards on four receptions.
text: Williams now operates as the clear change of pace option and preferred back in passing situations, with recent reports pointing to consistent pain due to a turf toe injury likely the culprit in the shifting dynamics of the backfield in Los Angeles. Either way, Williams spent most of the second half on the sideline as Corum set career highs in attempts (32) and yards (184) while becoming the first back in the Sean McVay era to reach 30 carries. Given the nature of the injury, this could be the new norm for a Rams team that continues to push for a postseason bid following a 2-4 start to their 20

title: Blake Corum rushed 32 times for 184 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 12 win over the Packers, adding 21 yards on two receptions.
text: The 184 yards on the ground easily set a new career high for the veteran back and his 32 carries marked the first time in the Sean McVay era where a single back ran the football 30 or more times, a mark that had not been reached since Todd Gurley over a decade ago. His trip to paint stretched his streak of touchdowns to five games while he also went over 100 yards for the second straight contest. The backfield split between Corum and Kyren Williams has taken a stark turn of late, with Corum now the preferred option on early downs and Kyren the preferred change of pace and clear passing situati

title: Matthew Stafford completed 16-of-23 passes for 140 yards and an interception in the Rams’ 26-13, Week 12 win over the Packers.
text: The two sides traded blows in the first half as the Packers came from behind to knot the game at 13 heading into the break, with Stafford leading three consecutive scoring drives to start the game for the first time this season. That was also the first time the Packers had allowed an opponent to score on three consecutive drives to start a game this season, but the departure of Christian Watson in the second quarter due to a concussion completely took the wind out of their sails in the second half. In total, the Rams attempted more runs than the Packers ran offensive plays (47 to 44), with thi

title: Tucker Kraft caught 3-of-5 targets for 24 yards in the Packers’ Week 12 loss to the Rams.
text: Kraft continues to look miles behind where he was during his breakout 2025 season before suffering a torn ACL, lacking burst out of routes while struggling through mental mistakes. Another such mistake appeared against the Rams when Kraft was stripped of the football in the first quarter following his longest reception in the game. The once-imposing Green Bay offense feel completely flat following the departure of Christian Watson in the second quarter due to a concussion, failing to score after the break while running just 44 total offensive plays. The Packers look to lick their wounds follow

title: Matthew Golden caught 1-of-5 targets for 39 yards in the Packers’ Week 12 loss to the Rams.
text: Golden found himself in lockdown coverage throughout, particularly following the departure of fellow receiver Christian Watson in the second quarter. The talented second-year receiver has seen double-digit targets in six of 11 games in his sophomore campaign and could be headed for another high-target game against the Saints in Week 13, pending Watson’s availability on a long week. Golden would be a legitimate WR1, should Watson miss, and an upside WR2, should Watson play. - Mark Garcia

title: Kaleb Johnson rushed eight times for 13 yards in the Packers’ Week 12 loss to the Rams, adding 19 yards on one reception.
text: The Packers were completely unable to run the football effectively against the stout Los Angeles defensive front, running just 44 offensive plays as they struggled to get any offense going following the departure of Christian Watson due to a concussion. Lead back Josh Jacobs appeared close to suiting up coming out of their bye and could make his way back into the starting lineup on a long week ahead of a Week 13 meeting with the Saints. - Mark Garcia

title: Jordan Love completed 17-of-29 passes for 198 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions in the Packers’ 26-13, Week 12 loss to the Rams, adding seven yards on one carry.
text: it was the second consecutive game with three turnovers for the Packers as two second half interceptions thrown by Love were a microcosm of the team’s inability to hang with the Rams without their top option through the air. Christian Watson departed in the second quarter with a concussion after being knocked out on a vicious hit down the sideline, leaving the Packers in a hole they could not climb out of despite taking a tied game into the break. It is possible for Watson to clear concussion protocol in a long week of preparation, but Love could realistically be without his top option when th

title: Lions declared CB Ennis Rakestraw, CB Keith Abney, S Chuck Clark, EDGE Tyrus Wheat, and EDGE DJ Wonnum inactive for Week 12 against the Bears.
text: - Zachary Krueger

title: Bears declared QB Case Keenum, CB Kyler Gordon, CB Isaac Yiadom, CB Elijah Hicks, RB Roschon Johnson, OL Jordan McFadden, and DL Jayden Loving inactive for Week 12 against the Lions.
text: Gordon and Johnson were both ruled out before this one, but the Bears are at near full strength heading into Thursday’s Thanksgiving Day tilt against the Lions. - Zachary Krueger

title: Colston Loveland was ruled out in Week 12 against the Lions after suffering a knee injury.
text: This is concerning. A Lions defender tumbled into Loveland’s lower leg left while the Bears’ tight end was blocking on a run play. After a brief trip to the trainer’s table, he was taken to the locker room for further evaluation. It took only 15 minutes for the team to rule him out. Before exiting, Loveland caught 1-of-1 targets for five yards and lost one fumble. On his lone catch, a Lions defender tied up his legs while a second defender ran in and punched the ball out of his possession. Since they are playing on Thanksgiving, the Bears have a few extra rest days before their Week 13 game ag

title: Colston Loveland was carted to the locker room in Week 12 against the Lions after suffering an apparent leg injury.
text: Loveland was tangled up, blocking against a Lions defender when another Lions defender tumbled into Loveland’s lower left leg in a classic roll-up mechanism. Both his ankle and knee could have been injured. Before getting onto the cart, Loveland sat on the trainer’s table with a towel over his head and appeared to be in considerable pain. We expect an update soon. - Nic Bodiford

title: Speaking with the Pittsburgh-Gazette’s Gerry Dulac, Steelers president Art Rooney II said Aaron Rodgers was not a “good teammate” following his release.
text: In a story published by Dulac on Thursday, Rooney said the Steelers are “100 percent” committed to head coach Mike McCarthy, while adding that “insubordination will not be tolerated” as far as Rodgers is concerned. According to Dulac, Rodgers and McCarthy met on Tuesday night, just hours before the QB’s benching, and presented McCarthy with an ultimatum: “let me call the plays or just release me.” What followed from there was Rodgers’ benching and eventual release after he went scorched earth on the Steelers and McCarthy on the Pat McAfee Show on Wednesday. Rodgers will be free to sign with an

title: Speaking on NFL GameDay Morning, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said Brock Purdy is considered day-to-day with his ankle injury.
text: Purdy suffered a sprained ankle in the Niners’ Week 11 win over the Vikings and was a DNP on Wednesday. Rapoport reports the injury is thought to be “minor,” but noted that whether or not Purdy suits up for Week 12 against the Seahawks “remains to be seen.” Given the importance of the divisional matchup, it’s hard to imagine Purdy sitting at this point. We’ll see how his next two practices go to close out the week, but this doesn’t sound like something we need to be too concerned about just yet. - Zachary Krueger

title: Steelers activated Michael Pittman (foot) from injured reserve.
text: Pittman is on track to play in Week 12 against the Broncos, catching passes thrown by Mason Rudolph. He is only a WR4/FLEX, given the circumstances. The Steelers also signed Max Hurleman to the active roster and placed receiver Ben Skowronek on injured reserve. - Nic Bodiford

title: Steelers placed Ben Skowronek on injured reserve with a calf injury.
text: Skowronek leaves the active roster while Michael Pittman (foot) makes his return. The Steelers also signed Max Hurleman from the practice squad to the active roster. - Nic Bodiford

title: Nick Herbig (hip/ribs) is not on the final injury report and will play in Week 12 against the Broncos.
text: Herbig is good to go. Steelers LB Alex Highsmith (ankle) and OG Gennings Dunker (knee) are ruled out. Steelers LB Cole Holcomb (heel) is questionable. - Nic Bodiford

title: Saints coach Kellen Moore said Juwan Johnson (hamstring) is day-to-day.
text: Johnson was not seen practicing today, so we expect to see him listed as a non-participant on the Saints’ official injury report. He looks like a long shot for Week 12 against the Bengals. Noah Fant is a TE2 with Johnson sidelined. - Nic Bodiford

title: Tyler Badie (thumb) is questionable for Week 12 against the Steelers.
text: Badie could return from injured reserve this week. The Broncos need an RB2 with JK Dobbins suspended for one game, but Badie would not be worth rostering in 12-team leagues, even if he fills that role. - Nic Bodiford

title: Cowboys declared TE Jake Ferguson, RG Tyler Booker, WR Jonathan Mingo, S P.J. Locke, DT Jonathan Bullard and LB Jaishawn Barham inactive for Week 12 against the Eagles.
text: Ferguson will miss another game with knee and ankle injuries. Brevyn Spann-Ford is a touchdown-dependent fantasy TE2 in his stead. Ryan Flournoy will likely beneift from Ferguson’s absence. Losing Booker, the Cowboys’ starting right guard, for this one is unfortunate. - Nic Bodiford

title: Amon-Ra St. Brown caught 7-of-10 targets for 146 yards in the Lions’ Week 12 loss to the Bears.
text: St. Brown shot out of the gates in this one, generating two explosive plays on the Lions’ opening drive. He needed a breather after being sandwiched between two Bears defenders on a deep completion on the Lions’ third drive. He played through a ribs issue a couple of weeks ago, and may reappear on the injury report with the same issue next week. Despite the hard hit, St. Brown stayed hot and continued ripping off long gains. A Bears defensive back committed pass interference against him on a target thrown to St. Brown right at the goal line. The ball fell incomplete, but the penalty setup one

title: Dallas Goedert (shoulder) has been ruled out for the remainder of Week 12 against the Cowboys.
text: Goedert suffered a shoulder injury on the first drive of the game and was ruled out a quarter later. The 31-year-old will get a week-plus to get healthy for Week 13 against the Cardinals, but for now Zach Ertz and Johnny Mundt will be the uninspiring tight end options. - Christopher Crawford

title: Jared Goff completed 25-of-36 passes for 313 yards, one touchdown and one interception in the Lions’ 35-39, Week 12 loss to the Bears, adding three rushes for 10 yards.
text: Goff’s first career Thanksgiving interception was not his fault. Jameson Williams tipped the pass right into Bears S Dillon Thieneman’s hands. Goff played very well on the day, and looked unstoppable whenever he targeted Amon-Ra St. Brown. Goff nearly tacked on a second passing touchdown on a trick-play pass to OL Larry Borom in the end zone, but the pass unfortunately fell incomplete. Goff remains a locked-in QB1 next week against the Falcons. - Nic Bodiford

title: Salvon Ahmed rushed three times for 50 yards in the Bears’ Week 12 win over the Lions, adding two receptions for 17 yards.
text: Ahmed provided the Bears with needed sparks on more than one occasion today, using his speed to initially rip off a 46-yard run on the Bears’ third drive. He later made a slick diving catch for a first down on the Bears’ 10th drive. He can be picked up in 14-team leagues at this time, though he is only a bench stash. - Nic Bodiford

title: Kyle Monangai rushed eight times for 15 yards and two touchdowns in the Bears’ Week 12 win over the Lions, adding one reception for 14 yards.
text: Monangai ran inefficiently this week, but that did not stop him from bullying his way into the end zone for a pair of short touchdowns. The burly back may still be rounding into form after his lengthy turf toe-related absence, but he remains a featured player in the Bears’ elite offense. Monangai is an RB2/FLEX against the Jaguars next week. - Nic Bodiford

title: D’Andre Swift rushed nine times for 65 yards and one touchdown in the Bears’ Week 12 win over the Lions, adding seven receptions for 97 yards.
text: Swift was extremely efficient on his touches against the Lions, which was good because the Bears got Kyle Monangai and Salvon Ahmed going in this one as well. Swift had two 30-plus-yard gains today. His first was a catch in the flats, which he took down the right sideline after juking two Lions defenders. The second was a clean touchdown run in which he faked right before cutting back to the left and outrunning the defense. He regularly operated as a needed checkdown option for Caleb Williams today. Swift is a borderline RB1/2 against the Jaguars next week. - Nic Bodiford

title: Saquon Barkley is questionable to return in Week 12 against the Cowboys with a stinger.
text: Barkley has struggled with just seven yards on five attempts, and was seen grimacing on the sideline before exiting the contest. With Barkley unavailable, Will Shipley will likely see the majority of touches. - Christopher Crawford

title: Caleb WIlliams told reporters that he was “fine” after undergoing X-rays following the Week 12 win over the Lions.
text: Williams said that he thought there was just a bruise on his abdomen after taking a fall. The signal-caller will get a mini-bye before the Bears take on the Jaguars in Week 13, and should be good to go for that contest. - Christopher Crawford

title: Denzel Boston (quad) was listed as a non-participant for Thursday’s practice.
text: That’s back-to-back missed practices for Boston. The 22-year-old still could be a go for Week 12 against the Raiders, but he’ll need to get in at least a limited session, and he doesn’t provide a ton of fantasy upside even if he does play for that matchup. - Christopher Crawford

title: Dallas Goedert (shoulder) is questionable to return in Week 12 against the Cowboys.
text: Goedert was injured on the first drive of the game and headed to the locker room. Zack Ertz and Johnny Mundt will likely see the majority of the snaps if Goedert can’t return. - Christopher Crawford

title: Sam LaPorta caught 4-of-5 targets for 44 yards and one touchdown in the Lions’ Week 12 loss to the Bears.
text: The Lions’ No. 1 tight end generated multiple double-digit gains today, including an 11-yard touchdown on a hitch-and-go just before halftime. He played through his ankle injury without issue after beginning the week limited in practice, notably diving to make a 17-yard catch. LaPorta is a TE1 against the Falcons next week. - Nic Bodiford

title: Jameson Williams caught 6-of-9 targets for 68 yards in the Lions’ Week 12 loss to the Bears, adding one rush for 12 yards.
text: The Lions got Williams involved on crossers, corners and screen passes today, but a few missed connections proved costly. Jared Goff targeted Williams in the end zone on the opening drive, but the pass fell incomplete. On the Lions’ fifth drive, Williams got behind the defense, but stumbled slightly, resulting in an overthrow instead of a long score. On the Lions’ 10th drive, Williams was unable to secure a third-down target at the Bears’ 25-yard line and accidentally tipped the pass to a Bears safety instead. That said, Williams deserves credit for generating a 39-yard gain on a corner route

title: Jahmyr Gibbs rushed 21 times for 205 yards and three touchdowns in the Lions’ Week 12 loss to the Bears, adding five receptions for 47 yards.
text: Gibbs is the most valuable player in fantasy football, regardless of format. Since scoring twice from one yard out isn’t enough for him, Gibbs ripped off a clean 70-yard touchdown run on the Lions’ ninth drive — and that probably wasn’t his most impressive play. One drive earlier, Gibbs took a run to the right side, and multiple Bears defenders broke past the offensive line. One got a hand on him, but he changed direction and took off for a 32-yard gain down the sideline. The impending 2026 league-winner should be treated as the overall RB1 in Week 13 against the Falcons’ beatable run defense.

title: Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle) is active for Week 12 against the Chiefs.
text: As expected, Kincaid will play after getting in a couple of limited practices ahead of the Thanksgiving showdown with the Chiefs. He should be treated as a lower-end TE1 for the contest. The Bills inactives versus Kansas City will be CB Christian Benford, WR Skyler Bell, S Jalon Kilgore, OLB Mike Danna, OT Jude Bowry and DL Greg Gaines. - Christopher Crawford

title: Chiefs declared RB Kenneth Walker, QB Garrett Nussmeier, CB Melvin Smith, DT Omarr Norman-Lott, T Diego Pounds, OL Jaylon Moore and DT Marcus Harris inactive for Week 13 against the Bills.
text: Walker will miss at least one more game while dealing with his groin strain, meaning Emmett Johnson should be the workhorse against the Buffalo defense. Nussmeier will be the emergency third quarterback. - Christopher Crawford

title: Carson Beck (back) will not play in Week 12 against the Commanders.
text: Beck will miss a second straight game with his back injury after missing all of practice this week. The rookie QB has dealt with back issues for the majority of the year, but will now set his sights on returning in Week 13 against the Eagles. That said, the Cardinals have a Week 14 bye, which could give them a reason to sideline Beck for at least one more week and let him heal up before returning for the final four games of the regular season. - Zachary Krueger

title: Josh Johnson will start for the Cardinals in Week 12 against the Commanders.
text: Johnson will get the start on Sunday against the Commanders in what will be a “revenge” game for the 40-year-old vet. Although, in fairness to Johnson, a lot of games are revenge games for the well-traveled vet. Things didn’t fare too well for Johnson in his first start of the season against the Chiefs, as he threw for 155 yards and one touchdown on the road, but did a good job of limiting turnovers. He’s nothing more than a QB3/desperation play in 2QB and superflex leagues. - Zachary Krueger

title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Colston Loveland (knee) is expected to land on injured reserve but “the current belief” is he could return later in the season.
text: The Bears are still running Loveland through additional testing and won’t make any final decisions to place him on IR until after those tests are complete, per Schefter. The early news of a sprained knee, however, is mostly good news for the second-year tight end. Loveland will be required to miss a minimum of four games on injured reserve and won’t be eligible to return until Week 18 at the earliest. title: Rams TE Tyler Higbee is considered week-to-week with a chest injury he suffered in Week 12’s win over the Packers.
text: ESPN’s Adam Schefter was the first to report the news on Higbee. Higbee will reportedly have “a chance” to play in Week 13 against the Chiefs, but as Schefter reported, that decision will be based on “how he heals over the next week.” Where things stand right now, the Rams are currently down three tight ends, with Terrance Ferguson (ankle) out for the season and Davis Allen (ankle) also considered week-to-week after going down in Week 12. title: Rams TE Davis Allen is considered week-to-week after suffering a high-ankle sprain in Week 12’s win over the Packers.
text: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport was the first to report the news. Allen will reportedly go to the Rams’ facilities today for a full evaluation to determine the approximate length of his absence, but with Terrance Ferguson (ankle) out for the season and Tyler Higbee (chest) also considered week-to-week, the Rams are suddenly very thin at tight end. Rookie second-rounder Max Klare and veteran Colby Parkinson are the only healthy tight ends currently on the roster, but it’s possible the Rams will look to add one or two more free agents to fill their needs at the position. title: Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle/groin) will not play in Week 12 against the Dolphins.
text: With a Week 13 bye on tap for the Jets, the team is hoping two extra weeks of rest will be more than enough for Cooper to play in Week 14 against the Broncos. Cooper has not played since re-injuring his ankle in Week 10 against the Bills and has now missed six of a possible 12 games in his rookie season. It’s possible this is the last update we receive on Cooper until the Jets return from their bye week, but fantasy managers in need of help over the next two weeks can safely drop him where needed. - Zachary Krueger

title: Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said he’s “not sure yet” if Bhayshul Tuten (foot/ankle) will play in Week 12 against the Titans.
text: Fantasy managers don’t need to panic just yet. The Jaguars have not taken the field for their Friday practice, and Coen said the team will assess how he looks on Friday before making any further decisions on his availability. Tuten has not practiced in either of the first two practices of the week, so a limited practice would be a slight upgrade for him heading into the weekend. We will check back in with a final update on his availability when the team announces it, but backup Chris Rodriguez could be in line for a busy week if Tuten were to be sidelined. - Zachary Krueger

title: Parker Washington (shoulder) will not play in the Jaguars’ Week 12 game against the Titans.
text: According to head coach Liam Coen, Washington aggravated an AC joint injury in Thursday’s practice that will sideline him for at least one week. Speaking with the media on Friday, Coen said the team hopes to have him back “ASAP” but noted that it is a “week-to-week injury.” Jakobi Meyers could be first in line to benefit from Washington’s absence, but this certainly isn’t an ideal situation for fantasy managers with the fantasy playoffs just weeks away. - Zachary Krueger

title: Dallas Goedert (shoulder) was spotted in a sling after the Eagles’ Week 12 win over the Cowboys.
text: Goedert exited Week 12’s win over the Cowboys with a shoulder injury on the first drive of the game. The veteran tight end did not return to the game, and the fact that he was wearing a sling after the game suggests this could be somewhat of a serious injury. Head coach Nick Sirianni did not comment on his injury after the game, so it’s possible we won’t learn until later next week what he’s dealing with and how much time he could miss, if any. title: Rashee Rice caught 2-of-5 targets for 19 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 12 loss to the Bills.
text: Rice’s quiet day was made all the worse by the refs when they overturned his third catch to an incomplete pass after replay showed the ball hitting the ground. While the tip of the ball did touch the turf, the ball didn’t appear to move. While the controversial call eventually led to a Buffalo victory, calling it a catch would have changed little for fantasy managers. Rice has played five games since returning from his early-season hamstring injury. He had more than 53 yards in just one of them. title: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said he had no update on Jeremiyah Love (ankle/IR) and would know more on Wednesday.
text: Love is eligible to come off injured reserve after this Sunday, but the fact that LaFleur won’t have a real update until Wednesday is probably foreshadowing that it will be at least another week. Love picked up a high-ankle sprain against the Cowboys in Week 8. - Rivers McCown

title: Jaguars coach Liam Coen said Parker Washington’s injury is “a big opportunity” for Josh Cameron.
text: You may have been thinking that Washington’s injury would create BTJ szn, but Coen singled out Cameron when asked about him, saying he’s “been trending. He’s made a lot of plays for this offense and for this team ... Trevor trusts him.” Cameron suddenly surfaces on the FLEX line as an expected Jaguars No. 2 target behind Jakobi Meyers against the Titans on Sunday. - Rivers McCown
